fields.label: Streaming enabled
fields.description: Master switch for the VBlank tile streamer. Turn it off to suspend all actor tile streaming (can also be changed at runtime with the 'Streamed Actor Set Enabled' event).

fields.label: Tiles uploaded per frame
fields.description: Maximum number of 8x8 sprite tiles copied to VRAM per VBlank. About 4 tiles fit in a DMG VBlank (8 at Game Boy Color double speed); past that the copy runs into the visible frame and holds off the LCD interrupts that set parallax scroll and hide sprites behind the overlay, which makes the background and the sprites flicker. In VBlank mode keep this at least as large as one frame of the sheet, since a frame is never split. In VRAM buffer mode it can be as low as you like - copies there are invisible until they complete.

fields.label: Tile update mode
fields.description: VBlank mode copies each frame straight over the tiles the actor is drawing from, so the whole frame has to be copied inside one VBlank. VRAM buffer mode reserves twice as many tiles per streamed actor and copies into the half the actor is not drawing from, then switches the actor over to it - the copy can be spread over several VBlanks without ever being visible, so a small tile budget is safe.

fields.label: Streamed actor slots
fields.description: How many actors can stream their frames at the same time. Each slot costs 14 bytes of WRAM.

fields.label: Use HDMA on Game Boy Color
fields.description: Copies tiles with general purpose DMA on a Game Boy Color - about 8 cycles per tile instead of 208, which is what makes the tile budget comfortable there. GDMA ignores the low four bits of its source address, so it needs the tile pool to be 16-byte aligned and is used here without checking whether it is: if your streamed actors draw scrambled tiles on a Game Boy Color, the pool did not land aligned, and turning 'Force aligned tile pools' on fixes it. Turn this off to always use the slow byte-at-a-time copy, which is correct either way. Has no effect on DMG builds.

fields.label: Force aligned tile pools
fields.description: Pads each shared tile pool out to a full ROM bank, so the bank packer has to give it a bank of its own. A pool that starts at the beginning of a bank is 16-byte aligned, which is what lets a Game Boy Color build move tiles with general purpose DMA - about 8 cycles per tile instead of 208. Without this the pools are usually aligned anyway, but nothing guarantees it. Costs whatever is left over in the last bank of each pool, up to 16 KB, and does nothing on DMG-only builds. Only applies in VBlank mode with 'Use HDMA on Game Boy Color' on - VRAM buffer mode copies from the render loop, where general purpose DMA cannot be used, and without HDMA nothing needs the alignment.
